newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives focus on employment as data loom.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives focus on employment as data loom.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives directed their election campaign assault on the Labour Party's employment policies on Tuesday, claiming a minimum wage and the European Union Social Chapter would cost countless jobs.

Economists said Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine and Social Security Secretary Peter Lilley were setting the scene for official jobs data, due on Wednesday, which are forecast to show another sharp fall in unemployment.
"It certainly looks like they are paving the way. We're looking for a fall of 50,000," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica.

A Reuter poll of economists produced a consensus forecast of a 45,000 drop in the number of jobless in March -- impressive, but more modest than some of the huge falls seen in the last few months. The data will be released at 0830 GMT on Wednesday.
Heseltine told a news conference that unemployment had fallen for four years under the Conservatives. "Labour's policies would destroy jobs," he said.
Tony Blair's Labour Party, unlike the Conservatives, is committed to introducing a minimum wage and signing the Social Chapter, which guarantees minimum employment rights.
Government ministers see statistics from the Office for National Statistics a few days before the official release, so they will know the figure already.
Philip Shaw, chief economist at Union Plc, also forecast a 50,000 fall in March. "The pace of decline in unemployment over the last couple of months has really picked up," he said.
Lilley warmed to Heseltine's theme. He said unemployment in most major European countries was "high and rising" in stark contrast to Britain.

"Other European countries follow the European social model with a national minimum wage and the Social Chapter," Lilley said. "If higher European unemployment is not caused by these policies...what does cause it?"
Elections are set for May 1 and despite a string of impressive economic data, Labour remains streets ahead in the polls although the gap may be narrowing.

Last month, 68,000 people were removed from the dole queues. That should have been the perfect starting point for the Conservatives' election campaign but sleaze stories capture the media's attention instead.

Tongue-in-cheek, Hawkins said everyone will know the figure from the Daily Mirror newspaper ahead of time. In each of the last two months, the Mirror has leaked the key unemployment figure, the first time getting it wrong but last month getting it exactly right.
